key_insight: A dilated causal CNN can detect charge jumps in superconducting qubits in real time, making radiation-event detection usable inside feedback control loops.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that offline qubit-diagnostic algorithms can be translated to low-latency FPGA firmware on QICK, enabling adaptive quantum hardware control with minimal delay.
method: Train a DCCNN on synthetic Ramsey tomography scans built from measured NEXUS qubit templates.
Deploy the model to FPGA using hls4ml with ap_fixed<16,6> quantization on a Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC ZCU216.
Use online inference to flag charge jumps during operation, with no per-qubit hyperparameter tuning.
evidence_signal: At 6.19 microseconds per inference, the DCCNN achieves detection efficiency comparable to the offline chi-squared method (0.843 ± 0.022 vs. 0.866 ± 0.020) at matched false-positive rate for |Δq| in [0.1, 0.5] e.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on synthetic training data and hardware-specific templates, so robustness to broader device variation and real in-the-loop operating conditions still needs validation.
paper_title: Real-Time Detection of Charge Jumps in Superconducting Qubits with a Convolutional Neural Network
